newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland signs deal with KGHM privatisation adviser.
newsitem.headline: Poland signs deal with KGHM privatisation adviser.

text.p: Poland's privatisation ministry signed on Monday a formal agreement with an international consortium to prepare the sale of the KGHM copper concern, ministry spokesman Jerzy Godula said on Monday.
"The agreement with the consortium was signed today," Godula told Reuters. He gave no further details.

A source close to the deal said that under the agreement the consortium of Union Bank of Switzerland, Barclays de Zoete Wedd and WBK brokerage had until the end of June 1997 to finish work on the privatisation.
The ministry picked the consortium in June, but could not start work on preparing the sale until the formal agreement was signed.
KGHM, employing 42,000 people, is one of the world's major copper and silver producers worth an estimated $2-$3 billion.
Under the ministry's tentative plan 10 percent of the company would be sold on the Warsaw bourse and some 15 percent would be floated in London.
Employees would be offered 20 percent while the state would retain five percent for reprivatisation claims.
However, the precise allocation of KGHM's shares as well as all other details of the sale are to be determined by the adviser.
